Quick one as we begin the Brightgate Whistic profile handoff. We ran into a couple small constraints on our side when wiring up presigned S3 proof uploads and wanted to confirm the lightweight flow you recommend for minimal-evidence customers. Specifically: 

- Best-practice TTL for presign links when upload is used as SOC2-derived proof (we typically see 1–24 hours depending on temp-cred model).
- Whether you can route uploads to a delegated-presign role so Brightgate keeps object ownership (we prefer Brightgate-owned buckets but want a minimal escrow posture).

For context: this is for the initial 100-customer batch; we want a minimal manual-review path (no full CAIQ in the first sprint) and a deterministic escalation for anything flagged in presign metadata.

Jordan —

Thanks for the clear ask. Short answers up front, then a recommended micro-runbook below. Happy to jump on a call if you want to walk through step-by-step.

- Presign TTL: we recommend 4–6 hours for upload-as-proof when customers are using ephemeral credentials. If you need same-day only evidence, you can go down to 1 hour, but risk increases for upload failures.
- Delegated-presign role: yes — we can configure a delegated IAM role that issues presigns while keeping object ownership in Brightgate buckets. That model is what our portal calls “delegated upload with custody.”
- Rollback: there is no literal revocation for a presigned URL once issued; best practice is to have a short lifecycle + a cleanup job that deletes objects not acknowledged in the evidence manifest within X hours. We also tag objects with upload-session IDs so you can run fast queries to remove bad uploads.

Micro-runbook (summary):
1) Issue presign with TTL=6h and upload-session header
2) Portal sends webhook to Redwood with session_id + manifest
3) Redwood acknowledges receipt within 30m -> mark proof accepted
4) If no ack after 6h, scheduled job deletes objects with matching session_id after double-checking manifest status
5) If evidence flagged by reviewer, follow the manual-remediation checklist (listed on page 2 of our runbook) which includes object quarantine and short-lived KMS rewrap.

I attached a short PDF (we'll put a canonical copy in the profile) but the above should get you started.

—Bethany
